from: July book, night 13 (The Axe Head That Floated)
p1: Some young men learned from Elisha, who spoke for Heavenly Father. They said, “Our home is too small. Let’s cut trees by the Jordan River and build more room.”
Elisha went with them. They chopped trees with axes, tools with heavy iron heads.
Splash! One axe head fell into the water and sank. The young man cried, “Oh no, master! It was borrowed!”
p2: He told Elisha right away. Elisha asked, “Where did it fall?” Then Elisha cut a stick and threw it in. The heavy iron axe head floated up! Elisha said, “Pick it up.”
Heavenly Father cares about little worries too. Tonight, think of one small worry, and tell Him about it in a prayer.
old: Elisha and his helpers were chopping wood by the river. They were building a new place to live and work. One man was swinging hard with a borrowed axe. Suddenly — splash! — the metal axe head flew off into the deep water.
The man felt terrible. “Oh no! That axe wasn’t even mine — I borrowed it!” He was worried because he could not pay for it. He didn’t know what to do.
Elisha asked, “Where did it fall?” The man showed him the spot. Elisha cut a stick and threw it in the water. Then the heavy iron axe head floated right up to the top!
Heavenly Father cares about big things AND little things. He helped with a lost axe head because His prophet asked. No worry is too small for God. He loves us and helps with everything.
